statement: For every complete finite simple strongly regular graph with parameters (99,14,1,2), let R count the actual nine-vertex subsets inducing the 3-by-3 rook graph, each subset once. Then R is not 229.

scope.description: Unrestricted target necessary condition excluding exactly the actual induced-rook count R=229. No exclusion of R=231 or of all target graphs is claimed.

assumptions: R is the count of actual induced nine-vertex rook subsets, not embeddings, row orderings or automorphism orbits.

steps: Reconstruct unique triangle-edge partners, the local defect graphs, D=6(231-R) and U=2079-9R.
At D=12, second-neighbor mass bounds force m<=2; complete weighted equality and square counts exclude m=2.
Exactly twelve positive triangles have deficiency one; their positive point multiplicities are even.
The fan-incidence count 12-r>=2r excludes multiplicity six without a cubic-dual assumption.
At multiplicity four, the eight remaining triangles each use one fan point; pair-common-neighbor limits force eight new points of multiplicity two.
Nondefective fan colors transport a rook to a required defect pair, so the new cycles alternate only between the two defect color pairs.
The two forced four-cycles each produce an induced rook across its fan defect pair, excluding multiplicity four.
Only now form the simple triangle-free cubic dual F on twelve triangle nodes and eighteen shared-point edges.
Uncovered target squares use selected triangle edges; induced squares of their line graph are exactly those uncovered squares, regardless of possible extra target edges.
C4(F)=18 saturates the cubic twelve-node bound; every component is K3,3.
Each K3,3 component is an actual induced rook containing a designated defect pair, a contradiction.
proof.operational_claim: No graph enumeration, matrix arithmetic program, source import or solver execution.

R229_reconstruction.multiplicity4_exclusion: Defect-colored four-cycle creates an induced rook
R229_reconstruction.equality_components: Two K3,3 components, forbidden by the defect rule

hand_boundaries.name: Two rook-nine graphs joined at a point
hand_boundaries.result: Twelve actual row/column triangles form an even selection with one multiplicity-four point; this refutes any unconditional multiplicity-two assertion.
hand_boundaries.why_not_counterexample: The selected triangle pairs are rook-covered, so the required all-deficiency-one condition fails.

hand_boundaries.name: Two abstract K3,3 components
hand_boundaries.result: The cubic twelve-node square bound is sharp at eighteen.
hand_boundaries.why_not_counterexample: The line graphs are rooks and violate the selected defect-pair requirement.

hand_boundaries.name: Hexagonal prism
hand_boundaries.result: Simple cubic triangle-free twelve-node graph with six four-cycles.
hand_boundaries.why_relevant: Cubic local geometry alone does not supply the necessary eighteen squares.

hand_boundaries.name: Multiplicity-four fan
hand_boundaries.result: Eight fan points force each remaining triangle to use exactly one; new-point pair common-neighbors force multiplicity two.
hand_boundaries.expected_first_contradiction: A forced four-cycle produces a rook containing a designated defect pair.

sharing: Root requested the multiplicity-four/six challenge and received the outline before freeze; this does not constitute independent approval.
limitations: R=231 remains possible on this proof.
No Makhnev, N3-free or global Hamming-cover conclusion is used.
No arbitrary binary right relation of weight twelve is excluded.
Possible actual extra edges on the eighteen-point support are not discarded; the uncovered-square bijection explicitly handles them.
No ledger, index, Git, historical candidate or execution gate is modified.
